title: Minimum Operations to Make Array Parity Alternating
summary: Given an integer array nums, determine the minimum number of operations required to make it parity alternating, where adjacent elements have different parities.
statement: Given an integer array nums, determine the minimum number of operations required to make it parity alternating, where adjacent elements have different parities. An operation consists of either increasing or decreasing any element by 1. The answer should include the minimum number of operations needed and the smallest possible range between the maximum and minimum values of the array after performing these operations. An array of length 1 is considered parity alternating.
constraints: nums is a nonempty integer array.
One operation changes one element by +1 or -1; first minimize operations needed for alternating parity.
Among minimum-operation results, minimize max(nums)-min(nums); return [operations,range].
hints: There are only two target parity patterns, and every mismatch costs exactly one operation.
For each pattern, count mismatches; changing an interior value cannot affect range, while a mismatched extreme should move inward.
Compute [operations,range] for both starts and take the lexicographically smaller pair.
This first minimizes operations; among tied patterns, inward moves attain the smallest possible extreme span, with a non-single alternating array having range at least one.
editorial: This first minimizes operations; among tied patterns, inward moves attain the smallest possible extreme span, with a non-single alternating array having range at least one.

tests.explanation: The best parity pattern needs two changes; choosing directions toward the interior gives final range six.
A singleton already alternates and has range zero, giving [0,0].
